experience.title: Automation Tooling Engineer (Staff Technician)
bullets: Quality pass cut an estimated 25% of drafting errors before licensed-engineer review.

Built a generator for standard details and grading from existing company drawing data. Applied it to the existing utilities model for an airport project, covering hundreds of thousands of surveyed entities. Hand modeling that took days fell to minutes.

Wrote Dynamo automation that reads Excel reports Civil 3D already generates and draws pipe flow levels and hydraulic grade lines. Other engineers verified the drop from about 8 hours of clicking to minutes.

Built a Civil 3D GUI for less experienced CAD users: color-coded IntelliSense-style layer and entity search with autocomplete, dynamic entity pull, and a local phrase-to-command lookup. From one command it moves entities, runs basic draw commands, retargets objects onto other layers, and otherwise edits uniformly across every layout instead of clicking through them in sequence. Minutes of that work, often hundreds of clicks, became one command that finishes in about two seconds. Found repeating bottlenecks in the firm's CAD workflow and wrote programs to remove them.
Built C# plugins against the Civil 3D .NET API to automate layout, audit drawings, and batch-rename title blocks. Attached typed metadata to Civil 3D objects so company standards sit on the entities.
Built OCR ingestion software that parses existing PDF plan sets, checks values, and populates drawings.

Built the firm's internal Civil 3D automation pipeline on the OpenAI API. It serves a user chat, scheduled batch jobs, and existing company drawing data as input for each request. A local Ollama model covers those commands when the API is unreachable.

Extended that pipeline to locate outdated sheet text and to compare design options. Authored and reviewed Git pull requests on the plugins and pipeline. Used GitFlow and trunk-based branching, resolved merge conflicts, and shipped through CI/CD.

Colleagues use the automation and generation tooling daily. Coordinates across civil, mechanical, plumbing, and architectural disciplines on named capital projects so one discipline's change does not break another's.

projects.name: Digital Twin Pro
projects.owner: Personal product - Free Parameter LLC. Not employer work, not built at or for David Mason & Associates.
projects.visibility: Public GitHub - released to a Google Play beta
projects.honesty: This is a personal product. Designed and built it for personal and business storage needs under Free Parameter LLC. It is not employer work. Went from concept to a Google Play beta in five weekends, about 10-12 days of actual work. Does not claim an LLM wrote most of the code. Photos are stored locally in the project folder. Does not claim per-user API quotas, DDoS protection, photo-moderation reporting, or immediately blocking a user: SecurityService is a stub that allows all operations, rate limiting is TODO, and Gemini harm blocks for those categories are set to none. Pays for the Google Gemini API. Does not claim download counts, revenue, ratings, or user numbers.
projects.summary: Built a Flutter 3D inventory product from concept to Google Play beta in five weekends. Custom painter's-algorithm renderer instead of a game engine. It features drag-and-drop totes on rack grids, including swap onto an occupied slot. Tote contents update by voice, photo, or typing from several screens. Spoken inventory is parsed to typed JSON maps. Custom QR codes encode contents and an optional photo path. Export one tote or the whole set as PNG, JPEG, or a multi-page PDF book for physical labels. Projects save, export, and import as folders. It uses Gemini photo capture, an AI Organizer that recommends like-with-like moves and previews them on the rack, QR books, and ARCore. A move log records each tote's from, to, and action. It runs on Android and Windows.
bullets: Architected the 3D renderer. Custom Z-sorted painter's-algorithm draw queue instead of a game engine.
Built drag-and-drop tote management on configurable rack grids, including swap onto an occupied slot. Used SQLite to store the inventory state model and move audit log.
Integrated the Google Gemini API for photo analysis. It detects items and quantities.

Tote contents can be updated by voice, photo, or typing from several screens: vocal quantities parses speech through Gemini into items, the camera runs photo recognition, and Edit Tote plus the database sheet take manual edits (with mics on description and quantity fields). All paths write one typed item-to-quantity map (integers or ~ estimates) shared by the tote, SQLite, and exports.

Custom QR codes encode tote JSON with toggleable fields (contents, quantities, items, colors, rack or floor position, optional photo path). Export one tote as PNG, or the whole set as PNG, JPEG, or a multi-page PDF book (QR plus location label per page) for print-and-stick on the physical bins. Cloud photo links are the next step on the photo-path field.

Saved each warehouse as a project folder with project_config.json, a project-scoped SQLite inventory.db, and photos stored locally in the project photos folder. Save, export, and import so the current job can be written out and opened again. CSV/JSON export and import are also available. Cloud photo links are not shipped.

Per-tote body and lid colors, or Apply style to all totes for a uniform look. Independent front and isometric frames (QR, photo, text, tote, or hidden). Three rack styles (metal, wood, plastic tube). Seven UI themes. Grid customization (rows and columns), with a location naming convention (letters on rows or columns, numbering from the base or the top) that relabels every slot.

Built an AI Organizer. Gemini recommends a short JSON plan of swaps and moves to group like with like (related items in the same zone). Preview animates those moves on the rack before commit; quick organize applies them immediately. The feature is experimental.
Move history is a deep log of tote transfers (action, from, to, tote label), not a field on the Tote row. SlotState also tracks which boxes have passed through a slot for evolved labels.
Used Firebase for auth and backend services. Used AppHive to release the beta build to the Play Store.
Added ARCore plane-tap placement on Android. Included seven UI themes, X-Ray mode, and emoji particle physics.
Used Provider state management across 64+ modules. Wrote about 33,000 lines of Dart across 103 files.
Shipped an Android APK/AAB with R8 obfuscation. Also shipped a Windows desktop build. Reached a Google Play beta from concept in five weekends, about 10-12 days of actual work.

projects.name: Integration bridge between a C++ desktop app and CAD software
projects.honesty: This is a local git repository with no remote. It is not a published repo. Third-party Dear ImGui and SDK headers are vendored dependencies. They are not original code.
projects.summary: Built a C++ desktop application. It drives AutoCAD, BricsCAD, and Civil 3D from outside the drawing editor. It sends commands and pulls drawing entities over Windows interprocess calls.
bullets: Built an interprocess integration layer. The C++ application sends commands and geometry requests across the process boundary. It pulls drawing entities back using Windows COM.
Hosted the same command path used at work: a plugin turns a written request into a command, then C# talks to the CAD host.
Wrote a toolchain that compiles and hotloads plugins in place. It locates installed CAD SDKs at runtime.
Wrote a translator that converts between script dialects. One command set targets multiple CAD hosts.
Wrote code to read and write drawing-database entities directly.
Deployed targets for BricsCAD, Civil 3D, and AutoCAD 2018. Included C# sample automations for sheet-set generation and room drawers.
Wrote about 14,000 lines of C++ and C# across 82 source files.

projects.name: Stormwater runoff calculator and drainage sizing model
projects.visibility: Professional work at David Mason & Associates - method described, client data withheld
projects.honesty: This describes the computation and the schema only. Does not publish client site names, drainage-area identifiers, elevations, or flow values. Does not store any client workbook in this repository.
projects.summary: Built a structured hydrologic calculator. It computes drainage areas, intensity coefficients, and runoff differential. It sizes storm structures. A CAD plugin can read and write its schema.
bullets: Computed runoff per drainage area. Split each area into pervious, impervious, and roof-direct surfaces. Applied an intensity coefficient to get flow.
Maintained coefficient sets per design storm. Sourced these from NOAA rainfall intensities for St. Louis. One model runs every required frequency.
Produced the total pre-development flow minus total post-development flow. The municipal stormwater review cares about this differential.
Sized storm structures. Computed head, sill, and high-water elevations. Tracked treated versus untreated disturbed area for water-quality compliance.
Embedded consistency assertions. They flag when pre- and post-development total areas stop agreeing. A transcription slip fails loudly.
Structured it as a template-driven schema. C# tooling can parse it and push results back onto drawing objects as custom metadata.

projects.name: Drawing-output standards comparison tool
projects.visibility: Professional work (David Mason & Associates) - method described
projects.honesty: This involves plot-style configuration only. Does not publish any client drawing content.
projects.summary: Built a tool to compare two sets of drawing-output rules line by line. It flags every difference. It prevents settings from silently drifting between projects.
bullets: Normalized two output-configuration tables into a common 255-row schema. This includes index, name, screening, line weight, pen assignments, and line type.
Cross-referenced both tables cell-by-cell. Raised a flag on any difference in screening, lineweight, or pen assignment.
Kept a lineweight catalog with inch-to-millimetre conversion. Can compare lineweights in either unit.
Turned a tedious manual comparison into a single review column. This made standards auditing across many drawing sets practical.

chunks.title: Project - CADNAT Bridge Studio
chunks.text: CADNAT Bridge Studio 1.3 is a local git repository with no remote. Built a C++17 Dear ImGui host. It uses COM to bridge BricsCAD, AutoCAD, and Civil 3D. It was a personal prototype of the architecture later used on a commercial deployment. Wrote a toolchain that compiles and hotloads plugins in place. Wrote code to locate installed CAD SDKs at runtime. Wrote a translator that converts between script dialects. One command set targets multiple hosts. Wrote code to read and write drawing entities directly. Deployed targets for BricsCAD, Civil 3D, and legacy AutoCAD 2018. Included C# sample automations for sheet sets, right-click menus, and room drawing. Wrote about 14,000 lines across 82 source files. Vendored Dear ImGui and SDK headers are third-party.

chunks.title: Project - BackupDeduper
chunks.text: BackupDeduper v1.2.4 is a local git repository with no remote. Built a C++17 phone-to-PC backup tool. Used SHA-256 content hashing so identical payloads are never copied twice. Wrote a backup engine with a copy-guard safety layer. Built an ADB bridge to Android with Windows-side phone path discovery. Implemented LAN HTTP transfer with a sync protocol and progress reporting. Backups never leave the local network. Built a Dear ImGui front end for Windows and Android. Wrote about 11,000 lines across 29 source files.

chunks.title: Project - offline CAD voice GUI
chunks.text: Built an experimental local voice-driven CAD command GUI in C++ with Dear ImGui. Wrote a command parser that turns recognized speech into CAD commands. Built a live autocomplete bar. Wrote an audio streaming module over miniaudio. Tried speech recognition with Vosk and whisper.cpp locally. It is entirely offline. There is no cloud speech API. This is a real working experiment kept in dated snapshot directories. It is not a packaged product. Vendored ImGui, miniaudio, whisper.cpp, and Vosk are third-party.

chunks.title: Project - CircleVisualizer
chunks.text: CircleVisualizer is a local single-file C++ math visualizer. Used OpenGL and GLFW with a Dear ImGui interface. Computed fifth roots of unity with std::complex. Plotted them on the unit circle. Traced simple harmonic motion as the projection of circular motion. Managed a small layer model. Each construction can be toggled independently. Wrote about 770 lines of C++.

chunks.title: Smaller projects, prototypes, and fluency
chunks.text: HatchCalc is an AutoCAD 2025 C# plugin skeleton. It has about 250 lines. PropertySetUpdater is a local sub-100-line Civil 3D command. It writes property-set values. The maintenance portal prototype is about 740 lines of React, TypeScript, Vite, and Supabase. It includes auth, a typed schema, and service-layer scaffolding. It is a prototype, not a finished portal. CBP document tooling is a cluster of small local C# WinForms utilities. Used Tesseract and iTextSharp for scanning manufacturing PDFs. Tensor visualization scenes are about 100 lines of Python and Manim. instant-ngp is a third-party tool runs on this workstation. Claims no original research.

chunks.title: Plain-language glossary - never answer with a bare acronym
chunks.text: I explain in plain terms first. I give the domain term second. GD&T is geometric dimensioning and tolerancing. It specifies how much a machined part can deviate. A CMM is a coordinate measuring machine. It measures a part's geometry precisely. MSD is the Metropolitan St. Louis Sewer District. It sets municipal stormwater standards. XData and property sets are custom structured metadata. They attach to CAD entities. An object stores typed data about itself. A quantity takeoff means computing material quantities from construction plans. ODS is a spreadsheet export format. A CTB is the table of drawing-output rules. It controls how a sheet prints. PPAP is the Production Part Approval Process. It qualifies a part for production. HatchCalc is an area-and-quantity calculator. It reads region geometry out of a drawing. CADNAT is an integration bridge between a C++ desktop application and CAD software.

chunks.title: What is not this code
chunks.text: Exclude these from the project list for honesty. Uses vendored third-party dependencies. These include whisper.cpp, Dear ImGui, miniaudio, Vosk, glad, GLFW, and arcore_flutter_plugin. Deploys third-party runtimes. These include Ollama, Open WebUI, and LM Studio. Did not write them. Uses cloned sample repositories. Has a tensor-demo directory that is a Python virtual environment. Has an empty ObjectARX skeleton with nothing to show.

chunks.title: This interactive portfolio site
chunks.text: This site is a resume portfolio. Built it with Vite, React, and TypeScript over an Express API. The public build is static and needs no backend. It generates a printable resume view and PDF from the same JSON data. An optional Express API can answer questions with a local Ollama model when it is running. The chat UI is currently disabled on the public site. Voice features are suspended. Containerized the optional inference stack with Docker for Linux, macOS, and Windows.

chunks.title: Git, pull requests, and CI/CD
chunks.text: At David Mason & Associates authored and reviewed Git pull requests on Civil 3D plugins and the automation pipeline. Used GitFlow and trunk-based branching, resolved merge conflicts, and shipped through CI/CD. Peer review is the quality gate before merge. Does not claim to have designed the firm's branching policy from scratch.

chunks.title: Prompt engineering
chunks.text: Uses Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Cursor. Does not call this applied ML or model training. Has not trained or fine-tuned a model.
